explanation: A physical or mental illness that weakens a person's health, here represented by the paralyzed man who was carried in to Jesus.
One word for a person with reduced mobility in their legs, often used to describe those who depended on others to move around.
An action or thought that goes against God's will and laws; Jesus shows here that he has authority both to heal the body and to forgive sins.
The act by which a debt is wiped out, something Jesus demonstrates by declaring the sick man's sins forgiven before healing him physically.
The rightful power or authority that Jesus exercises to give commands concerning health and moral purity in God's name.
A profession in which one catches fish, here used to describe the background Matthew had before following Jesus.
A person who collected taxes on behalf of Roman rule; often viewed with contempt in a Jewish context because they collaborated with occupiers and were accused of fraud.
A religious ritual where one abstains from food, used by the disciples of John the Baptist as a sign of repentance or expectation of the Messiah's coming.
A participant at a wedding feast; Jesus uses this image to say that his presence is a time for joy and celebration, not mourning and fasting.
A piece of fabric that has not yet been washed or used; in the parable, it shows how God's new grace can ruin old religious traditions if they are mixed together without care for the whole.
